summary: All seven findings confirmed; five fixes are completed or adjusted. /1: ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 5 plans the weak embedding problems and the H² obstruction; route 7's brief must import it too, and route 1 must also supply that the class of the pulled-back extension is ρ*α. /2: the connecting maps and their compatibilities are built at the pinned Tau Ceti (DiscreteShortExact); exactness is built as well, Q and Q/Z need discrete copies, and ∂₂(χ) = χ*(θ) stays a missing step. /3: the §5 matrix groups are built, but the orders of B_n and U_n are not. /4: CDT25 route 7 (accepted) makes D7 the owner of the finite-group universal coefficient theorem; D7 should plan the general form, and the maintainer should weigh a more foundational owner. /5: the witness H = A = ℤ/2 over ℚ is right; keep /128's 'no claim of necessity' (sharp is not necessary) and add the sharpness item. /6: all five misprints confirmed, plus a sixth (Lemma 4.1, sum to k for r). /7: the AMS page shows the version of record was revised on 7 March 2025 and cites four works absent from v1.

That text says nothing about universal coefficients: D7 owns them only because of the accepted CDT25 route. In the MS26 extraction, /52, /53 and /123 are in route 6. PAPER-WOOD-19/131 ('For a group F and trivial coefficient module A … 0→Ext¹(H₁(F,Z),A)→H²(F,A)→Hom(H₂(F,Z),A)→0') is in route 8, a Part II of InductionRestriction named InductionRestrictionPartIIReducedSchur, and its review accepts that route. Nothing else supplies the theorem. The Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology README has no universal coefficient theorem. The ClassFieldTheory README mentions Tor₁^Z only as the hypothesis of Tate–Nakayama. Mathlib 082e2d3 has a Tor bifunctor (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Tor.lean) but no universal coefficient or Künneth theorem, and Tau Ceti f790474 has none either. Mathematically, all three are one theorem: the universal coefficient theorem for a complex of free abelian groups, applied to the standard resolution P of G. CDT25's homology sequence is its tensor–Tor form for Z⊗_G P. CDT25's Ext isomorphism and Wood's H² sequence are its Hom–Ext form. MS26's /52 is the tensor–Tor form for the cochain complex Hom_G(P,Z). When G is finite, this is a complex of finitely generated free groups, so Hom_G(P,X) = Hom_G(P,Z)⊗X; that is where finiteness enters, and /123 is the case of free X. Section 15 requires such a notion to be planned once, in the most general form its uses need, by one owner. The duplication is therefore a genuine breach of §15. On the fix: moving /52, /53 and /123 into a source route with stages ['ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7'] is right. It is exactly how both papers come to cite one owner: MS26 becomes a second source for the owner that has already been accepted, and route 6 imports from it. The other way round would mean reopening CDT25's accepted route, which is outside this extraction. There is no cycle: D7 requires only R02.1, R02.2 and R02.4, and route 6 already imports R02.2. Four refinements to the fix. (1) The planned form should be the general one. D7 should plan the universal coefficient theorem for complexes of free abelian groups and derive three sequences: (a) the homology tensor–Tor sequence, for any group; (b) the cohomology Hom–Ext sequence, for any group and any trivial A, since Wood needs an arbitrary group F; (c) the cohomology tensor–Tor sequence from integral cohomology, for finite G (or G with a resolution by finitely generated free modules), with arbitrary trivial X and with /123 for free modules of any rank. The finding's label 'Ext/homology form' for CDT25 is loose: CDT25 has a Hom–Ext statement for cohomology and a tensor–Tor statement for homology. (2) The route 6 brief must name ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 among its imports, beside R02.2. /54 (Lemma 3.4) stays in route 6 as the consumer. (3) /53 (Tor₁^Z(C,−) preserves injections because Tor₂^Z = 0) is a fact about Z-modules, not about groups. It should still move with /52, because the owner of the theorem fixes the Tor₁^Z interface, on Mathlib's existing Tor carrier. (4) The maintainer note should record a cost. D7 has depth 5 and requires R02.4 (Poitou–Tate), so with D7 as owner, a purely algebraic lemma pulls Poitou–Tate duality into the dependencies of the negligible-classes Part II, Wood's Schur Part II and CDT25's noncongruence Part II. Section 15 prefers the most foundational owner. The maintainer may therefore choose the pending ProfiniteCohomology Part II design as the single owner instead, re-pointing CDT25 route 7's item and Wood /131. What matters is that there is exactly one owner. The owner should also import the algebraic core rather than prove it again. Tau Ceti's AlgebraicTopology README, stages 5–6, already plans the Künneth and universal coefficient sequences over PIDs for degreewise-free chain complexes. The quotation is right. On the page image of p. 4 (§1.4, after Theorem 1.3) the paper says: 'When A acts trivially on H, the subgroup of negligible classes was determined by Gherman and the first author in [GM22], without assumptions on primitive roots of unity. Their result implies that the assumption on roots of unity in Theorem 1.3 is sharp.' The TeX agrees, in the paragraph after thm-negligible. H̄² is defined after (3.7) on p. 12: it is the subgroup of H²(H,A) generated by the images of φ_{H′} = cor∘∪ : A^{H′}⊗H²(H′,Z) → H²(H,A), over all subgroups H′ ≤ H. The proof on p. 13 says Theorem 1.3 is equivalent to H²_neg,F = H̄². The extraction has no item for the sharpness claim, and the word 'sharp' appears nowhere in it or its report. The GM22 prerequisite's 'why' leaves out GM22's classification, and /70's note gives no example. I checked the witness myself. Take H = A = Z/2 with trivial action. Then e(A)e(H) = 4 and lcm(e(A), e(H)) = 2. First, H̄² is everything. The subgroup H′ = 1 contributes nothing, since H²(1,Z) = 0. For H′ = H, A^H = Z/2 and H²(Z/2,Z) ≅ Z/2 is generated by c = ∂χ. Cupping with a ∈ H⁰ is the coefficient map n ↦ na, so 1∪c is the reduction of c modulo 2. That reduction H²(Z/2,Z) → H²(Z/2,Z/2) has kernel 2H²(Z/2,Z) = 0, so it is injective. Since H²(Z/2,Z/2) ≅ Z/2, H̄² = H² ≅ Z/2, generated by a class α. Here c is the class of 0→Z→(×2)Z→Z/2→0, whose pushout along Z→Z/2 is Z/4, so α is the class of 0→Z/2→Z/4→Z/2→0. Second, α is not negligible over Q. Let ρ: Γ_Q → Z/2 cut out Q(i). Then ρ*α = 0 exactly when ρ lifts to Z/4. Such a lift would be surjective, and would send complex conjugation, an element of order 2 with ρ(conj) ≠ 0, to an element of order at most 2, that is to 0 or 2. Both map to 0 in Z/2, a contradiction. Equivalently, ρ*α = (−1,−1) ≠ 0 in Br(Q)[2]; GM22's Lemma 2.7 gives ∂x = (x,−1). So H²_neg,Q = 0 ≠ H̄², although Q contains μ_2 = μ_lcm = μ_{e(A)} = μ_{e(H)}. The witness is correct. The paper's appeal to GM22 is as the finding describes. The finding cites the GM22 author PDF with SHA-256 2fecf5a1…, and the quotation from its p. 2 is exact. The proof of GM22's Theorem 5.2 says 'Applying Corollary 3.4 in the case m = 2 we see that H²(G,Z/2Z)_neg = 0 since t = 1', that is, whenever √−1 ∉ F; this covers the witness directly. In the body of that PDF the classification is Theorem 4.2; Lemma 4.1 is a lemma about towers of roots of unity. The introduction's 'Theorem 4.1' is GM22's own slip. Theorem 4.2(1) gives the whole sharpness claim. Take H = Z/p^a and A = Z/p^s with trivial action, where a, s ≥ 1, and F = Q(μ_{p^{a+s−1}}), so that t = a+s−1 ≥ s. Then H²_neg,F = (H*[p^{a−1}] + p^sH*)/p^sH* = pH*/p^sH*. This is strictly smaller than H*/p^sH* = H̄²; by the projection formula, corestrictions from subgroups add nothing when the action is trivial. So μ_{e(A)e(H)/p} does not suffice, which is what 'sharp' means. Two changes to the fix. (1) The finding says /128's note ('Keep the primitive mn-root hypothesis; no claim of necessity') records 'the opposite stance'. It does not. That note is about the hypothesis of Example 2.2, and it is true: 'sharp' is not 'necessary'. For H = A = Z/3 and F = Q(ζ₉+ζ₉⁻¹), F contains no primitive cube root of unity, yet F(ζ₃) = Q(ζ₉) contains μ₉. Theorem 1.3 over Q(ζ₉), together with GM22's Corollary 2.4 ([F(ζ₃):F] = 2 is prime to 3), gives H²_neg,F = H² = H̄². Keep 'no claim of necessity' and add the pointer to the new item; do not replace it. The new item's note should say that sharp does not mean necessary. (2) The prerequisite's 'why' should cite GM22's Theorem 4.2 (called Theorem 4.1 in its introduction), Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 3.4, not 'Theorems 4.1 and 5.2'. Optionally, the new item can state the paper's claim itself, with the Q example as the elementary test and the cyclic family as the general proof from GM22. The rest of the fix is right: the name, locator and statement of the new item, routing it to route 6, and the acceptance test beside /64. Medium severity is fair, since this adds a negative test that guards the hypothesis e(A)e(H).

I checked each slip on the page image and in the TeX. (i) p. 4 image: 'When A acts trivially on H', where A is the H-module; 'H acts trivially on A' is meant. (iii) p. 8 image, proof of Lemma 3.2: 'Consider the étale F-algebra M := L[t]/(t^n − f)'. The setting of §3 on p. 7 has only K and L. M is finite étale over L, since n is invertible in K, and hence over K. The proof then works with Aut_K(M) and with M/K as a Galois G-algebra, so 'étale K-algebra' is the smallest correction. (v) p. 17 image, proof of Claim 5.6: 'By definition, H̄²(N, A) is generated by the images of all the φ_H, where H is a subgroup of U'. Each φ_H has target H²(U,A), and the claim concerns res^U_N(H̄²(U,A)), so H̄²(U,A) is meant. /95's note records this. None of the five is already registered. E1 is Lemma 4.1 (pp. 12–13, its hypotheses), E2 is (2.3) on p. 6, E3 Lemma 2.5 on p. 7, E4 Proposition 3.3 on p. 11, E5 Lemma 5.3 on p. 15, E6 Claim 5.7 on p. 19, E7 Claim 5.7 on p. 18, and E8 Example 2.2 on p. 5. REV-PAPER-MERKURJEV-SCAVIA-26.md says: 'Remark 5.8(1) also prints "in in". That is not registered.' (p. 19). Section 18 asks for every mistake found to be recorded, so the finding is right.
